name: Corrupt Primal of Air

facts.text: The four Corrupt Primals rise at the waterfall bridge after the voices; Olcasgean wakes only when all four are dead. Their shared line is 'We shall protect.'
Level 83 with only 900 health; it flies, never melees and never walks home. Pets and turrets deal a fixed 5 per hit; direct damage kills it.

story:
The wind of Hy Brasil was the first of the four to be taken, the Sylvan say, because wind goes everywhere and so went down into the hollow before anything else. The Root kept it. Now it circles high over the bridge, a little knot of stale air that has forgotten how to blow. It has almost no body to wound, and it knows it: it never comes down to fight, never closes, never flees, only hangs there while its kin do the killing. Beasts and summoned things claw at it uselessly, for there is nothing to claw. A single honest spell of the right weight will scatter it. The trick is to remember it is there.

The Sylvan remember the wind of Hy Brasil as a gentle thing. It carried seeds and rain and the smell of the sea, and on still days it went down into the earth through every crack and cave, because wind goes everywhere. That is how the Root caught it. It went down into the hollow one summer and did not come back up, and the forests had a dry year after, and then a dying one.

What hangs over the bridge now is the wind's memory of itself: a knot of stale air with the Root's voice in it. It is the first of the four to speak when strangers come, and the weakest to strike, and it knows both things. So it never comes down. It hangs above the fight and watches its kin do the killing, and it waits for the raid to forget it. Beasts and summoned things claw at it and find nothing to claw. One honest spell from below scatters it. The Sylvan say that when it dies a breath of clean wind crosses the bridge, and that those who feel it should say thank you, because the wind was a friend once.
legend: Air goes first and it goes fast: one good nuke from below kills it. Pets and turrets are useless on it, so send them at the others. Casters and archers look up the moment the primals spawn. Forget it and it will hang over the bridge all night while its kin do the killing. Mages and archers should have a target on it before the others have finished rising. If a raid loses its casters early, a single archer can still do it; it is the cheapest kill of the night and the most often forgotten. The Sylvan ask one thing: when it dies, feel the clean wind, and say thank you.

aggro: The wind remembers nothing but the Root.
A whisper of stale air: we shall protect.
The wind that went down and never came back.

loremasterTopic.text: The wind of the isle, taken first and kept longest. It barely has a body. One true spell scatters it; claws and pets find nothing.

bookPage: From Aodhan's notes in Domnann: the Sylvan have a little prayer for wind, said at seed-time, asking it to carry the seed and come home. They say it every year still, though the wind they prayed to went down into the hollow long ago. When I asked why, the fire-keeper said: because it might hear. The realm's raiders tell me that the guardian of air has almost no body at all, that a single spell undoes it, and that a breath of clean air crosses the bridge when it goes. I told the fire-keeper. She went outside and stood in the doorway for a long time, with her face to the night, and said the prayer again.
